title: Gaucher disease
summary: Gaucher disease happens when the body lacks enough of an enzyme that breaks down a fatty substance. The substance builds up, mainly in the spleen, liver and bones.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the GBA1 gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier has one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually do not know they are carriers until they are tested.
disease_meaning: A person with two changed copies has Gaucher disease. It varies a lot: some people have mild signs, others more serious ones. Treatments exist for some types and are given by specialist teams.
screening: A carrier test uses a blood or saliva sample. It looks for the most common changes and cannot find every possible change.
suggested_questions: Someone in my family has Gaucher disease. Could I be a carrier?
Can Gaucher disease skip a generation?
What does a test for the GBA1 gene involve?
card_summary: A fatty substance builds up in the spleen, liver and bones. Carriers are healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. Can affect the spleen, liver and bones; treatments exist for some types.
care: Specialist metabolic and haematology clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
